lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is the San Miguel County BOCC, which holds public hearings on three Land Use Code amendments Wednesday — including changes to how 'Qualified Owner' is defined in affordable housing rules, a wildfire overlay update, and a continued hearing on nonconforming lots, all moving toward formal votes. Also Wednesday, the Telluride Housing Authority Subcommittee takes up a real case: a deed-restricted homeowner seeking approval to replace a roof that runs well above the 5% capital improvement cap. Mountain Village's Design Review Board considers conditional-use permits and initial reviews for three multifamily projects Thursday, and Ouray County's Planning Commission works through possible Land Use Code definition changes in a virtual session.

notable.stake: Public hearings on three Land Use Code changes, including affordable housing ownership rules.
Vote on whether a deed-restricted owner can exceed the 5% improvement cap for a new roof.
Conditional-use permit and architecture reviews for three Mountain Village multifamily projects.
Land Use Code definition changes that could quietly reshape what rules allow in Ouray County.
